_about: Investigation playbooks. Each lists what the server checks (only approved reports), what the data can never establish on its own, and the focused next question. No figures live here.

playbooks.title: Collections went up or down
checks: Insurance versus patient payments, this period against the one before
Payments by payer, this period against the one before
Payments by practice, this period against the one before
Claims processed, as the volume context
Claim status counts, as the denial context
cannotEstablish: Whether payers processed claims more slowly (no payer processing dates in the reports)
Whether payments were posted late rather than received late (posting date is the only basis used)
Which claims a payment belongs to (payment-to-charge allocation is not validated)
Whether a payer changed policy or stopped paying for a reason
next: Compare claim submissions by payer for the same periods
Look at claim status counts by payer for the largest-moving payers
Open the largest-moving payer or practice month by month

playbooks.title: Insurance A/R went up
checks: Insurance A/R today by payer and age
Charges and payments for the period as the flow into and out of A/R
cannotEstablish: How A/R moved over time: the source keeps no history snapshots
Which payers' balances grew: there is no prior balance to compare to
How much of A/R is denied money: no approved source for denied dollars
next: Compare payments with charges for the last two months
See which payers hold the oldest balances
Ask for historical A/R snapshots to be kept so movement can be measured

playbooks.title: Denials went up
checks: Claim status counts, this period against the one before
Claim status counts by payer, this period against the one before
cannotEstablish: Denied dollars: no approved source or definition
Whether denials are new or older claims being re-worked
next: Open the payer with the largest increase month by month
Look at the reasons recorded for that payer
Compare resubmissions for the same payer

playbooks.title: A payer stopped paying
checks: Payments by payer, this period against the one before: payers with payments before and none now
Claim submissions by payer, to see whether claims stopped going to that payer
cannotEstablish: Why the payer stopped: the reports hold no payer correspondence or processing dates
Whether payments are only delayed rather than stopped
next: Compare claim submissions to that payer
Check claim status counts for that payer
Contact the payer once the data shows when claims were last paid
